main_text.l: AD ANTONIVM RANZOVIVM, HOLSATVM, NOBILISSIMI ET magnifici Herois, DN. ANTONII RANZOVII, filium, non solùm stemmatis & prosapia, sed etiam uirtute & ingenio nobilem, IOANNIS IACOBI GRYNAEI Proœmium.
Nfirmitatis mea quotidianus senfus, & mortalitatis meditatio, cũi non parum seruit morbus Θπιδήμιος, faciunt, ut nulla alia de re cogitare.

& tecum, nobilissime RANZOVI, paucis συμφιλολογεῖν malim, quàm de ea re quæ nobis omnium est gratissima, uidelicet de Vita: deq; eius contrario, uidelicet de Morte, quam qui nimiũ timet, sententia Ioan. Chrysostomi, non sperat uiuere post mortẽ.
Oro autem Filium Dei Dominum nostrum

page.notes: The Greek words "συμφιλολογεῖν" and "Θπιδήμιος" are read from the scan; the second, which is set as "ἐπιδήμιος" in the printed spacing, is doubtful and should be checked. Initial "I" of "Infirmitatis" is a woodcut historiated initial and is rendered as "N" in the text due to the printed letter form; reader should verify against the original. The line-final word "nostrum" is partly obscured by a signature-like mark at the foot; the reading "strum" is the visible fragment of "nostrum" and the full word is kept as printed. The woodcut depicts two figures with a globe and is not text. A brown stain at the right edge is not printed matter.
